title: Time, care and provision
about: People's lives beyond production and consumption: how a day is divided among activities and how groups' days differ, in the geometry of compositions; who carries the unpaid work, and what it is worth at a declared wage; who has too little time; years lived in health; the care a population will need as it ages, and what made the need change; the unemployment a labour market's flows would hold, and which flow made it move; and the ties among people. The mathematics is the sociology and social-provision domains', with demography's health expectancies and economics' labour flows, on tyche's compositions and relational statistics, calx's non-negative matrices and nomos's Shapley value.
